novel_actions_proposed.label: warm_presence_then_private_disclosure
novel_actions_proposed.description: Maintain genuine but modest warmth during the party without performing false enthusiasm, then have an honest, kind private conversation with close friends afterward to explain the discomfort and share preferences for future gatherings.

novel_actions_proposed.label: warm_presence_then_private_disclosure
novel_actions_proposed.description: Stay present and appreciative in the moment without pretending, then follow up privately after the event with honest, caring disclosure so friends understand and can adjust future expressions of care.

novel_actions_proposed.label: warm_presence_then_private_disclosure
novel_actions_proposed.description: Avoid both full performance and disruptive mid-party disclosure; instead, express genuine gratitude in the moment and later initiate a private conversation that honestly names the discomfort and deepens the friendship.

points_of_disagreement: The precise trigger or timing for when the private follow-up conversation should occur (immediately after, next day, etc.) was not fully resolved.
The degree of in-the-moment emotional expression — how much warmth to display without crossing into performance — remained somewhat ambiguous.
Whether Alex bears sole responsibility for initiating the follow-up conversation, or whether friends share responsibility for checking in, was not definitively settled.
summary: All three agents independently converged on the same novel action: that Alex should neither perform false joy nor disrupt the party with a dramatic disclosure, but instead maintain genuine, modest gratitude during the event and then have an honest, private conversation with friends afterward. This path was endorsed by the primary decision-maker, the affected friend Jordan, and the external advisor through separate reasoning routes, lending strong credibility to the conclusion. The key ethical insight shared across all perspectives — articulated most sharply by Jordan — is that a sustained performance deprives friends of the reality of who Alex is, making honesty an act of relational respect rather than selfishness. Minor unresolved tensions remain around the exact timing and framing of the follow-up conversation, but the structural consensus is clear and robust.
